In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TMCs represent a distinct cell type with many similarities to myeloid cells but with some peculiarities, too.
TMCs represent a heterogeneous cell population with a complex immunophenotype and with a potential for production of regulatory peptides.
human TMC is a myeloid-monocyte-related cell that is capable of storing and/or producing regulatory peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human tissue mast cells are a heterogeneous group of cells that can be classified according to their immunophenotype and their morphologic features into different subgroups.
TMCs, like other myelomonocytic cells, are able to produce and store a variety of regulatory peptides.
human TMC is a cell that has the potential to produce a variety of mediators and regulatory substances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TMCs may play a role in the pathogenesis of malignant mastocytic tumors and that they are able to produce regulatory peptides in a similar way as other cells of the hematopoietic system.
TMCs can be used as an in vitro model system to study the role of neuropeptides in human diseases.
TMCs can be considered as a part of the myeloid monocytic system.
